messages:
cheng: FYI I ran a perf sampling + flamegraph pass on the latest serving build after enabling the new batching heuristic. Saw an odd hotspot on the CPU side that looks like repeated small wakes in the batch coordinator.
alex: Can you drop the commands and the flame link?
maria: also which commit/branch and config? could be the heuristic backoff we added.
cheng: Branch: release/1.3.0-collection. Config: batching.window_ms=8, batching.max_inflight=32 (default kv-cache enabled).
cheng: Perf command I used:
```
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./bin/redwood-serving --config ./tests/prof/batch-config.yaml
sudo perf script > out.perf
./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf > collapsed.txt
./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl collapsed.txt > flame.svg
```
cheng: Attached flame.svg (uploaded to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 — flame shows a repeated ~7-10ms slice dominated by python3:/redwood.runtime.batch_coordinator._poll_loop and then a small native spin in futex_wait.
jamie: interesting — does the flame show python frames at the top of the stack? that suggests GIL hold or frequent ctypes boundary.
cheng: yeah top frames look like:
- PyEval_EvalFrameEx
- runtime.batch_coordinator._poll_loop
- runtime.batcher._try_dispatch
then native:
- futex_wait
- pthread_cond_timedwait
so seems like we alternate between python scheduling and kernel wait.
alex: Could be we're creating lots of small timers instead of a single epoll loop. Any trace of epoll_wait vs select?
maria: Also check that we're not calling into Python from the fast-path kernel selection. If kernel selection calls back into Python (model registry lookup) we'll pay huge overhead per request.
cheng: I dumped a perf top summary and the sample counts:
- python (PyEval...) 38%
- libc futex_wait 12%
- runtime C++ batch_enqueue 9%
- kernel_selector (C++) 6%
So Python dominates.
jamie: Did you run with sampling frequency 99? might overrepresent PyEval if we hit Python in the timer check. Try increasing -F 997 for better distribution and re-run.
perf-bot: perf run completed: samples=2.1M duration=120s cpu=all (report: https://perf.redwood/profiles/2142501123).
cheng: good call — I re-ran with -F 997 and added a perf trace focusing on callchains. New run shows similar shape but the Python frames are concentrated in a small helper: runtime.utils._compute_next_deadline (Cython wrapper) which calls into time.monotonic() and does a formatted logging call under debug.
alex: aha, formatted logging in the hot path. Are we logging at DEBUG for every batch poll?
cheng: yes, debug log: logger.debug(f"batch wake: size={len(q)} deadline={deadline}") inside _poll_loop. When I disabled that logging the Python % dropped to ~12%.
maria: patch that to debug-once or aggregate metrics. Also consider moving monotonic/time checks into C++ side or use eventfd + epoll to avoid periodic sleep/wake.
jamie: Also check the batching.window_ms=8; with very small window we may be waking too often causing more Python scheduling. Try 12 or 16ms and measure tail latency.
cheng: did a quick A/B: window=8 -> p50 token latency 28ms, window=16 -> p50 30ms but CPU usage dropped ~22% and tail p99 improved slightly for concurrent 100qps.
cheng: I pushed a small PR that: 1) removes per-iteration debug log, 2) moves monotonic() call out of Python hot loop into a thin C++ helper, 3) introduces a single epoll-based waiter for batch coordinator. Patch: https://git.internal/redwood/serving/pulls/985
alex: can you include a microbenchmark showing the change? e.g. synthetic harness with 1-5ms token lengths and batching enabled.
cheng: yes adding microbenchmark + perf flame comparisons to the PR. Plan: land as a canary on cluster-staging, enable for 5% of traffic, watch CPU samples and tail latency dashboards.
maria: Also add a regression test that runs perf smoke in CI? maybe just a lightweight CPU sample to catch obvious backslides.
jamie: SGTM. One more ask: add a note in runtime/README about avoiding formatted logging on hot-paths and how to use the C++ helper.
cheng: done, will update PR with docs and a follow-up perf run in the thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
